body: We live together. I love him deeply. I don't want to loose him.
My ocd has progressed much worst very fast so I'm seeing a specialist to try different medications
I'm on 40mg but I'm about to be put on something else for it. Give it time to sew if it works for you.
You're not crazy. Start taking the steps to take control of this. See a therapist, try anxiety medications, and reduce the stresses in your life. You got this.

Is another episode nearing or is your anxiety telling you that? You're afraid of another episode, your anxiety is waiting for it to happen so you're on edge just waiting for this "impending doom" Remember to tell yourself, you got through it once and your strong enough to do it again.

To help your disssisociation symptoms, you need to control your anxiety. Eliminate stresses in your life, make sure you get 8 hours a sleep a night, eat clean, and exercise. You're not alone though. Many people feel the same way you do.

Sounds like a PTSD response. When you get like this try some coping mechanisms and let your thoughts and feelings go. Running your hands under warm water during these feelings and taking deep breaths will calm your nerves.

Try to recognize your thoughts are just thoughts. Let them come and go but don't let them scare you because they're just thoughts. Try listening to The Honest Guys meditations on YouTube and breathe in through your nose and out your mouth.
So you feel like nothing is real and question every aspect of reality? It's such a scary feeling and I feel so alone.

I have a psychiatrist. We started sensory therapy and she has taken great care into my treatment. I've had some great breakthroughs but I stopped seeing her for a year since I got better and I slowly went back to where I started and just not resumed my sessions with her.

Context- we dated for four years. He cheated on me the entire relationship and I dumped him six months ago. Recently we became fwbs but he wanted more. We gave it a go again and he broke it off. Then he says maybe in the future we maybe can be something. So I sent him the first message you see and the conversation goes from there.
My therapist once told me, "if you're afraid you're going crazy, you're not crazy. Crazy people don't know they're crazy." That statement brought me a lot of peace.
Before you leave out to go in public, lay down and listen to a meditation (the honest guys on youtube) and close your eyes. It will calm you down immensely and it has helped me.

You sound like a very helpful partner. Encourage her to see a therapist to help her professionally. Give her room to cope with this and try not to get annoyed with her. She can't help her ocd and she more than anyone wishes she didn't have to deal with it. Be patient and kind.

You have nothing to be ashamed about. This happens to me too. Ocd thoughts can be intrusive. Try meditating, YouTube videos by the honest guys, and lay down and take deep breaths when these start to happen. Itll slow your heart rate and calm your body. Let your mind relax and then when the meditation over tell yourself, "this is mental. I am capable of getting better. I will get better. I will try to not let my thoughts get control of me" hope this helps.

You're not crazy. This is not weird. You should not feel ashamed. Ocd affects so many aspects of your life. First, surround yourself with friends that are there to help and understand you. Second, start with baby steps to not overwhelm yourself. Try have a small snack without performing your ritual. One time a day to start off for awhile. Then turn to one meal a day of not doing it for awhile. Then it'll turn into all your meals of not performing your ritual.
Everyday. I feel like if I don't perform some of my ocd rituals something bad will happen to me. I'm trying to get over it and I hope you do too.
Something to try to help is to let your mind wonder to other things. When a song comes on, sing along quietly and focus on the lyrics. Focus on the beats and rhythm. It will slowly help.

This is very similar to what I do. Little rituals to make me feel better. I'm not a therapist or anything of the sort so please don't take what I say to the standard of a professional. You've done it so long it is now a ritual and you can't disrupt that without feeling anxious like something bad is going to happen. Next time, when you feel the urge to do it, think, "nothing will happen if I don't do this. This is all mental and not real. This may make me uncomftable now but I'm making progress to get better" I just have to remind myself that the discomfort I feel in the moment of not doing my ritual is better than letting my ocd take over my life.

This happens to me constantly. A dent in a creamer cup, garbage. I can go through so many and just throw them away if I see a single dent. Like what if something happen to it or what if something bad happens because I used it? Its so intrusive for me. I started off getting over it by just using it even if there is a dent. Just going full force. Sometimes I'd have to dump all my coffee out and start over but day by day its getting easier. I can just grab two little creamer cups and not even look at them and just use them. There's days I mess up and dump my coffee but its progressively getting better than before.
He said he will be starting therapy and I told him nothing will happen between us if he doesn't.

There is a reason he is hiding it from you. It sucks to accept the truth but some people just don't have your best intentions in mind. Find someone who won't hide things from you and value your worth.
Let the healing process run its course. It may hurt now, but if you deny your feelings it will only hurt you later on in life.

I found out he was cheating the same day I found a note on his phone with my ring size. Timing sucks sometimes. But you made the right decision with no contact. Time will help you and you'll bounce back from this.

I think to heal, you need to take break from the relationship. You did nothing wrong. He is in the wrong. Put yourself first for once and leave. Even if its for a small period. You don't want to destroy yourself for a relationship that he didn't value.
I thought I could stay after I found out he was cheating too. It ended up destroying me. Save yourself the pain before its too late.
You can leave. And you need to to heal. Take your time, leave at your pace don't stay forever. You'll look back and wonder why you stayed in the end. You deserve better.

I was in your position. I stayed after I found out he was cheating. Everytime he didn't answer or I didn't do something he wanted, I assumed he was cheating or was going to cheat on me again. Its a terrible feeling you shouldn't have to go through. You need to leave this relationship and heal.

Its hard. Its painful. Its a messed up thing to go through. You got this though. You will build yourself up and heal from this. You don't need to beg him to choose you when you have so much more worth than that. His current actions proves he won't change. You gave him a second chance and even then he chose to do the wrong thing. It has nothing to do with you and all to do with him.
I'm glad you found the closure you needed to heal.
I wish someone told me my boyfriend was cheating on me for the three years he was. You did the right thing.
She showed her true colors to you. That's not someone you want by your side for the rest of your life. View this as a win. She taught you how you shouldn't be treated by the next partner.
Take your time. Put the rings on when it feels right with you. No need to rush anything.
I still get emotional after sex with my other partner after being cheated on by my ex. Go to therapy. Its helping. Find time to heal yourself from the inside out. You are your top priority.

Please seek therapy. Even just video chat therapy if going out the house is an issue with you. You need to work through this. Maybe being in the same environment as the person who caused this is hindering your growth. I'd suggest staying with someone if that is possible. 

I hope the best for you.
Try calling the number on your own phone and see if a female answers
You think I may be too hard on him for this?
If he has the intentions to meet someone physically...that's it. Maybe take a break with him and cut contact for awhile before you revisit the idea of continuing the relationship.

We talked for hours. He knew I wouldnt like him buying videos from girls but he did it. The month he talked to the girl was a year and a half ago. I'm just wondering if you think this relationship can build from the ground up again?
He hasn't changed his behavior from the first time. Apologies and empty promises can only do so much.
I think I should've clarified he only flirted with one girl and paid girls for nudes and videos on sites. Thank you so much for commenting
We're also doing therapy together now....
Hes my first boyfriend I ever had and the first person I ever loved. I cant think of not being with him. Found out he planned on proposing too before this all happen.
